text.title: Product Development Trends Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the request is a category scan or a verdict on one already-chosen tool, whether a change window exists this cycle, and what shape the reachable adoption evidence has — to a full scan, a decline-only reduced scan, a pre-work fix, or a skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Is a category of tooling and practice in scope, or has one tool already been chosen and the only open question is adopt-or-not?

branch.when: one named tool is already chosen and the question is whether to adopt it

conclusion.verdict: skip: this is an evaluation, not a scan — run a time-boxed spike or a bake-off against the incumbent and score that one tool directly

branch.when: the team is under six months old and has not stabilised a baseline stack

conclusion.verdict: skip: `applicability` has no codebase to price against, so every entry would be a generic fit statement

branch.when: a category is in scope but the stack is frozen by contract or certification, or there is no engineering capacity to change tooling this cycle
branch.question: Does a change window open inside the artefact's own shelf life, and does the current stack contain anything with a published support-end date?

branch.when: no window this cycle or next, and nothing in the stack has a dated support end

conclusion.verdict: skip: the scan can only produce a wish list — re-open it when a change window exists

branch.when: the window opens next cycle, or at least one dependency already carries a published end-of-life date

conclusion.verdict: run a reduced scan: the decline and end-of-life track only — dated support ends plus migration targets, no new-adoption candidates until capacity exists

branch.when: a category is in scope against an established stack the team can change this cycle
branch.question: What adoption evidence is actually reachable for the candidate trends?

branch.when: only vendor press releases, funding announcements, star counts and all-time download totals

conclusion.verdict: stop before drafting: replace every cumulative counter with a period-over-period rate (monthly downloads, weekly active dependents, release cadence) or drop the candidate — a monotonic metric cannot emit the decline signal the scan exists to catch

branch.when: share-over-a-population series exist, but no dated external maturity assessment covers the candidates

conclusion.verdict: run the scan but leave `hype_curve` null until a Thoughtworks Technology Radar ring with volume number, a Gartner Hype Cycle edition, or two adoption metrics moving in opposite directions can be cited

branch.when: adoption is sourced, but at least one candidate is pre-GA (preview or beta) with no published stable API or config contract

conclusion.verdict: record release status, licence and any recent licence change, and the vendor's deprecation record for adjacent products; pre-GA candidates are marked hold regardless of adoption score

branch.when: candidates are GA with sourced adoption, but at least one alters build output or on-disk formats with no export path

conclusion.verdict: price the reversal, not only the entry: name the files, CI definitions and retraining touched, then mark any one-way door `hold` even where the adoption score is high

branch.when: each candidate has a share-over-a-denominator series with a named population and date, and a dated external maturity ring

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: sourced adoption signals, externally anchored hype phase, release-status record, exit-priced applicability, and at least one decline or end-of-life item from the team's own stack
